Our Trust
Fairchildes Academy Community Trust
A very warm welcome to Our School
At Fairchildes, we are all about Inclusion. We believe that with opportunity, support and encouragement our children can achieve anything. We want our pupils to have a love of learning, to be enthused and excited about every lesson. We want them to be sociable, friendly and empathic; to be good citizens; to speak and perform with confidence in every situation. We want our pupils to love coming to school! We aim to give our children every opportunity to succeed. This includes employing additional support staff to ensure that every child is successful in every lesson; running additional provisions such as Oracy groups and fine motor sessions; employing specialists to give the children the very best teaching of art, music, dance and PE; expanding opportunities through additional trips; running a successful Able Gifted and Talented programme as well as a multitude of after school and holiday clubs.
We have a dedicated, hard-working and talented staff. Our children are expected to behave well and there is a strong sense of mutual respect that they demonstrate within the school community. We place an emphasis on developing skills for life, confidence, independence and a sense of responsibility and most importantly, achieving this in partnership with our parents and carers.
We are very proud of our outstanding school and its achievements.
You are welcome to come and visit us at any time to see us in action.
Mark GyfordHead of School

Breakfast Club
Fairchildes Breakfast Club has been running for many years and aims to inspire healthy eating as well as encouraging children in the importance of eating a meal before the school day.
Children are invited to come into school at 7:30am. There are many games and fun activities for all ages to take part in, ranging from ICT, board games and construction to sewing and gardening. This allows children and parents/guardians the opportunity to socialise and build friendships with peers, easing into the school day within a relaxing atmosphere and environment. Staff are on hand with any enquiries or help that may be needed.
There is a breakfast menu that offers something for everyone at a reasonable price and this is served from 8:00am.
Breakfast Club also has many special events which take place throughout the year. We celebrate different occasions including Chinese New Year, The World Cup, Christmas, Easter, Mother’s Day, Valentine’s Day, St George's Day and many more.
It’s a fun, fabulous way to start the school day, come and join us.
Prices for Breakfast Club are as follows:
7:30am - 8:45am - £3.00
8:00 am - 8:45am - £2.00
Places at Breakfast Club need to be booked and paid for in advance on ParentPay but if you have any queries please don’t hesitate to speak to Mrs Howland or email bc@fairchildes.croydon.sch.uk. All pupils and family members are welcome at Breakfast Club.

Reading
Reading with your child
The most important thing when reading with your child is that it is an enjoyable time to spend together. This can only be achieved if does not become a chore to you or your child, but a relaxing time when your child has your full attention. To aid this:
At Fairchildes we use the ELS phonics scheme. This teaches the child the sound for each letter/letters they see so that they can split the words into the sounds they make and then blend them back together to read the word. This is the way most children will learn to read and tackle unfamiliar words.
If they are stuck on a very difficult word or on a name, it’s okay to just tell them the word rather than let them struggle with it.
The most important thing for your child is to understand and discuss what they have read, even if they struggle with the decoding. For most children, it is the vocabulary in a book that they may struggle to understand, so it is vital to discuss word meanings. Below are some of the types of questions you might ask whilst you are reading to encourage your child to think about what they have read and to have an opinion. They are just to get you started, but as long as you are talking about the book you are making them think about it. If your child is unsure of the answer then give your opinion so that they can learn how to respond to questions asked.
Please follow the links below to view advice for reading in specific year groups.

SEN Information Report
September 2025 - July 2026
Pupils with Special Educational Needs at Fairchildes September 2025 - July 2026
Children receiving SEND support
The current range of disabilities within Fairchildes
The school has children with a range of disabilities which include Autistic Spectrum Disorder, ADHD, MLD, Hearing Impairment, Visual Impairment and physical needs. Some pupils have medical conditions such as Epilepsy, Chronic Allergies and Sickle Cell Anaemia. When children enter school with specific disabilities, the school liaises with LA professionals & previous settings for assessments, support and guidance for the school and parents/carers.
We have a number of children who have asthma and all staff are aware of these children. Inhalers are kept in the classrooms and a record of use is noted.
Some children have allergies or food intolerances/cultural food choices. We have our own independent caterers who are able to meet the needs of children with specialist diets in an inclusive environment. Some children also use specialist cutlery.
All medical information is collated and available to the relevant staff, with a designated member of staff responsible for their monitoring.
All medication is kept in a central safe and secure place which has easy access for First Aiders and staff members. Consent forms for the administration of medicine are filled in by parents, outlining the condition and dosage of medication. All medication that is given is recorded.
How has SEN been identified at Fairchildes this year?
When a child is making significantly slower progress than their peers or is struggling to achieve their predicted potential they could be considered to have Special Educational Needs (SEN). Early intervention is essential for progress however it is important to avoid mislabelling a child with additional needs and to remain focussed on meeting their needs.
In partnership with the Class teacher, SENCO, SLT and parents we considered any barriers to learning.
Barriers could include:
We know that children who experience these types of barriers may be vulnerable students but this does not mean they should be identified as a child with SEN.
The learning of all children at Fairchildes Primary School is regularly and rigorously assessed.
Data meetings were held termly and progress and attainment was monitored. Additional support was put in place to support children who had been identified through the progress meetings.
The SENCO/SLT followed up with children who had received QFT and additional support in school and had not made expected progress.
The Educational Psychologist was able to support teachers in developing or adjusting their practice for targeted children who were identified with significant special educational needs.
Inclusion meetings were held each half term and the information collected was used to support assessments regarding whether a child had additional needs.
Senior leaders regularly reviewed children’s work through book looks, data meetings and observations within each year group and fed back to individual teachers. Through this process individual children were identified for further support.
The three schools within the FACT Trust moderated across all year groups during the Autumn and Spring Term.
Formal Assessment was also used to identify needs:
Children were added to the SEN register if their ability was significantly below their peers and a short-term barrier could not account for their lack of progress or attainment. Parents were involved in decision making and reviews of decisions were held regularly.
This year has seen a continued rise in referrals to CAMHS and since September 2024, nine referrals have been submitted. In addition, four requests for referrals have been submitted to GPs for neurodiversity assessments.

Provision for children in school
Better Days SALT Services have been commissioned to provide speech and language therapy support for pupils with EHCPs and initial speech and language assessments for children from Reception to Year 6.
Better Days therapists provide in-school support and review progress for pupils within our Pathways provisions, as well as for pupils with EHCPs in our mainstream school. Our Communication Coordinator works alongside therapists in both the 360 and Encompass provisions, supporting review meetings and intervention sessions.
For new referrals within the mainstream setting, the current waiting time for Better Days SALT services is approximately 2–3 weeks. Referrals are submitted online by our Communication Coordinator.
NHS speech and language therapists contribute to needs assessments for children who are undergoing the EHCP assessment process.
During the summer term, all Nursery children were screened using the Little Link online programme. This helped us to identify children who would benefit from additional speech, language and communication support, allowing us to put appropriate SALT interventions in place at an early stage.
Our Communication Coordinator also continued to deliver the ICAN Talk Boost programme to a KS1 group. All children participating in the group made good progress.
Throughout the year, all Reception children have had access to weekly language groups, with children identified as requiring additional support attending more targeted daily sessions.
Nursery children have also benefited from twice-weekly language and communication support groups, helping to develop their understanding, vocabulary, listening and communication skills.
In-school OT support has been provided to individuals and small groups throughout the year. This has included the Funky Fingers programme and targeted sensory programmes for identified children who needed additional support to develop their fine motor, sensory and self-regulation skills.
School staff have also implemented recommendations from previous OT assessment, ensuring that strategies and approaches are embedded into one child’s daily school routines and provision.
Encompass children received Occupational Therapy input through their EHCPs, following the NHS OT service moving to clinic-based appointments only. One child received an OT assessment during the Summer Term, and two children received OT support from Sterling OT Services.
Checking-in sessions have continued throughout the year, with requests for support coming from parents, children, teachers or social care when needed. Mentors have provided 1:1 mentoring and small-group sessions in the Mentors’ Room, offering children a safe and supportive space to talk, regulate and develop strategies to manage their emotions and relationships.
Our mentors have also provided support to families, particularly in response to the challenges created by the cost-of-living crisis. They have supported families experiencing emotional and behavioural difficulties at home, providing practical and emotional support as well as signposting families to appropriate services and sources of help.
Alongside their direct support for children and families, our mentors have continued to run the pre-loved uniform shop.
5 children have received regular counselling sessions during the year.

Training and Development 2025-2026
We have an extensive staff at Fairchildes who continuously look to develop their practice and extend their expertise. An ongoing programme of training is in place to ensure that teachers and support staff have appropriate skills and knowledge.
This year training has included:
Equipment and Facilities
Fairchildes has extensive resources to meet the needs of children with SEN (see our school offer). This year we have continued our use of augmented technology to include: iPads, reading pens and laptops as well as using software such as Times Table Rockstars and Communication in Print (Widgit).

You can contact any of these members of staff through the main school switchboard - 01689 842268Contact Mr Gyford directly - ht@fairchildes.croydon.sch.uk
Which outside agencies have been accessed through Fairchildes?
The use of outside agencies very much depends upon the individual needs. However, some are frequent visitors to school.
1. The Educational Psychologist
This year our EP has been Dr. J Lawton. She has made regular visits to school this year.
2. Speech and Language Therapy
Children with EHCPs in the 360 Centre have had their speech and language needs met during regular visits from a variety of therapists. The Communications Coordinator joins them in therapy sessions, reviews as well as providing support for 360 children.
3. Occupational Therapy
The OT from Sterling visits the Encompass ASD ELP to review targeted children as well as providing advice to the staff and their parents.
4. Locality SEND Support Scheme
Fairchildes has continued to be part of the Locality SEND Locality Support Scheme this academic year. Fairchildes has also received support for SALT assessments and EP advice. The locality scheme has seen schools in the area benefit from closer working practices that has supported the transition for children going to high school.
5. CAMHS/Community Paediatrician
We refer children to CAMHS or to the community Paediatrician for concerns regarding their mental health or for a diagnostic assessment of ASD and ADHD. Referrals are also made for Emotional Well Being Support via CAMHS.

Young Carers
Our whole school is committed to meeting the needs of young carers so that they can attend and enjoy school in the same way as other pupils and achieve their potential. The school only shares information with professionals and agencies on a need to know basis in order to support pupils and their families. Fairchildes actively seeks feedback and ideas from young carers and their families to shape and improve support.
Fairchildes has a designated Young Carers’ School Lead with responsibility for young carers and their families. The current lead is Nicky England who can be contacted at school via phone : 01689 842268 ext 3.
The Young Carers’ School Lead oversees the day-to-day operation of the school’s Young Carers’ Policy, coordinating provision for children who are Young Carers.
The Young Carers’ School Lead is a role within the Inclusion Team. The Inclusion Team can offer further support for young carers.

Attendance
As part of our commitment to improving the attainment of our pupils, we monitor pupil attendance on a regular basis to help support families and resolve any issues that may cause children to be unnecessarily absent from school.
In order to encourage good attendance at school, we raise awareness by:
We hold termly attendance awards for children that achieved 100% attendance during a school term. Where possible, we make allowances for children that have missed 100% attendance by one morning or afternoon session (provided that the absence was authorised by the school.) We also take into account individual circumstances, such as when a child has made a special effort to attend school as much as possible alongside having a specific medical need.
We understand that children may be absent due to illness during the school year. If your child has missed the 100% award for a term due to illness (e.g. chicken pox, vomiting and diarrhoea), please do not be discouraged as eligibility to attend future awards starts again from the next term.

Sleepover: Children will take part in games throughout the evening before going to bed in sleeping bags in the school hall. Snacks and hot chocolate will be served in the evening and breakfast will be served the next morning.

100% attendance achieved in the Spring Term
Burger and Bouncy Castle Night: Children will take part in outdoor activities, such as Connect 4 and hula hooping. Burgers and drinks will be served.

Online Safety
CEOP helps any child or young person under the age of 18 who is being pressured, forced or tricked into taking part in sexual activity of any kind. This can be something that has taken place either online or in ‘the real world’, or both. The CEOP Safety Centre has clear information and advice on what can be reported to CEOP, the reporting process and what will happen if you do decide to make a report. You can visit the CEOP Safety Centre and make a report directly to CEOP by clicking the Click CEOP button. If you are experiencing online bullying or something else online has worried you please speak to an adult you trust, or you can talk to Childline at any time on 0800 1111 or at www.childline.org.uk.

What we do
Our Parent Teacher Association (PTA) plays a vital role in supporting the Fairchildes community. With a shared goal of enriching school life, we work together to raise funds through exciting, inclusive, and fun opportunities for all our pupils.Every penny raised by the PTA goes directly back into the school, benefiting our children and helping to make Fairchildes an even better place to learn, grow, and build friendships. The funds we generate enhance resources, support activities, and create memorable moments for every child.We organise a wide range of fundraising events throughout the year, as well as events simply designed for fun and community spirit. These include: • Mufti Days • Crazy Hair Day • Summer Fetes • Easter Egg Raffles • School Discos and Silent Discos • Christmas Fayre • Christmas Gift Wraps • Easter Bonnet Parade • Raffles and moreOur events bring together pupils, families, and staff, creating a strong sense of community while making a real difference to the school.We are always delighted to welcome new members and volunteers—whether you can help regularly or just occasionally, your support makes a big impact!

Reach More Parents & ParentPay
RMP
Our school communication system is called Reach More Parents (provided by Weduc). Every family joining Fairchildes Primary will need to download this app to be able to access the important information the school makes available. This is where parents receive school messages, letters and give consent to activities. Please contact the school office if you are having issues logging in or require an invite code.
The benefits of this system:
Attach photos of medical appointments.
Receive messages from school.
Every parent has their own private logon.
ParentPay
All payments at our school are made through ParentPay, an online payment system for schools. It allows parents to pay quickly and securely for school meals (if applicable), Breakfast and After School Club and trips and activities.
You can simply top-up your ParentPay account online by debit or credit card. Your ParentPay balance can be used immediately to pay for any of your children’s items at school.
Please click the link below to access ParentPay and contact the school office if you are having issues logging in or require an invite code.

School Meals
Our kitchen staff are always available to discuss the menus with you. If your child has an allergy please drop in and see a member of our Kitchen Team, they will do their utmost to accommodate your child's needs.
Bread, Salad Cart, a selection of Fresh Fruit, Low Fat Yoghurts and Vegetarian Jelly are also available daily in addition to the changing menu items.
All primary school children in London in Reception - Year 6 are entitled to a free school lunch this academic year.
To check if you are eligible for free school meals please follow the link below and answer a few, very simple, questions. Every child eligible for targeted free school meals brings in more money to the school, which is spent on resources to support our children. We are most grateful to those of you who have done this.
